title: When a dam blocks salmon: a fish ladder
subject: Life science

sources.title: NGSS 3-LS4-4: Make a claim about the merit of a solution to a problem caused when the environment changes
NOAA Fisheries: Adult upstream passage on the West Coast

steps.title: River
steps.instruction: Trace the water on both sides and the riverbed.

note.text: Salmon hatch in rivers, swim to the sea, then return upstream to the same river to lay their eggs.
note.remember: Salmon must swim upstream to have young.

steps.title: Dam
steps.instruction: Trace the dam across the river.

note.text: People build dams to store water and make electricity. But a dam is a wall the salmon can't swim past: their environment has changed.

steps.title: Fish ladder
steps.instruction: Trace the steps beside the dam.

note.text: A fish ladder is a set of water-filled steps. Salmon swim or leap from pool to pool to climb past the dam, resting in the pools.
note.remember: A ladder lets fish climb over a dam.

steps.title: Salmon
steps.instruction: Trace the salmon waiting below the dam.

note.text: Salmon are strong swimmers and jumpers, which is why ladders work well for them.
Salmon use smell and other senses to find their way back to the river where they hatched.

steps.title: Route
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow showing the salmon's way up the ladder and over the dam.

note.text: The flowing water at the bottom of the ladder attracts the fish and guides them in.

steps.title: The problem
steps.question: Why could fewer salmon live in this river after the dam was built?

options.text: The dam blocks them from swimming upstream to lay eggs
options.feedback: Yes. If adults can't reach their spawning grounds, fewer young salmon hatch each year.
The problem is the wall itself: it blocks their path upstream.

options.text: The dam makes the water too cold
options.feedback: The main problem is that the dam blocks the way upstream.

options.text: Salmon live only in the sea
options.feedback: Salmon need rivers too: they lay their eggs upstream.

steps.title: Judge the solution
steps.instruction: Think about what each idea solves.
steps.question: Which solution best helps the salmon while keeping the dam working?

options.text: Build a fish ladder beside the dam
options.feedback: Yes. Salmon can climb past, and the dam still stores water and makes electricity. Engineers design each ladder to suit the kind of fish.
That would help the salmon, but people would lose the water and electricity. A ladder solves both problems.
That makes the wall even harder to pass. Salmon need a way around it.

options.text: Add more fish below the dam
options.feedback: They still couldn't reach their spawning grounds upstream.
